chosen_translation: I need to go to the post office.
rejected_translation: To me there is needed the post.
defect_description: Dative 'мне нужно' requires English 'I need'; 'почта' in this context means post office.

chosen_translation: I like this city.
rejected_translation: To me this city is pleasing.
defect_description: Dative 'мне нравится' requires 'I like'.

chosen_translation: I need a certificate from the clinic.
rejected_translation: To me there is needed a reference from the polyclinic.
defect_description: Dative 'мне нужна' requires 'I need'; 'поликлиника' is clinic; 'справка' is certificate not reference.

chosen_translation: The queue is moving slowly.
rejected_translation: The queue moves slow.
defect_description: Verb 'moves' needs adverb 'slowly', not adjective 'slow'.

chosen_translation: The document submission window is closed.
rejected_translation: Window of accepting of documents is closed.
defect_description: Articles missing and double genitive 'of accepting of documents' is ungrammatical.

chosen_translation: The passport expired two months ago.
rejected_translation: The passport is overdue by two months.
defect_description: 'Просрочен' for documents means expired; 'overdue' is for payments.

source: Штраф нужно оплатить до конца недели.
chosen_translation: The fine must be paid by the end of the week.
rejected_translation: The fine must be paid to the end of the week.
defect_description: Deadline expressed with 'by', not 'to'.

chosen_translation: The application is processed within five working days.
rejected_translation: Application reviews during five working days.
defect_description: Article missing; 'reviews' should be passive 'is processed'; 'during' should be 'within'.

chosen_translation: Please sign here.
rejected_translation: I respectfully request that you affix your signature to the designated location herein.
defect_description: Routine administrative request uses polite imperative, not elaborate formal phrasing.

chosen_translation: Take a number!
rejected_translation: I instruct you to obtain a numbered ticket from the dispenser!
defect_description: Practical instruction at a service counter uses short imperative.

chosen_translation: The red tape wore him out.
rejected_translation: Paper red-tape tired him out.
defect_description: 'Бумажная волокита' maps to 'red tape'; 'wore him out' is the natural result.

chosen_translation: The case has been dragging on for a year.
rejected_translation: The case is pulling for a year already.
defect_description: 'Тянуться' for cases means to drag on; present perfect continuous required.

chosen_translation: The report was drawn up according to all the rules.
rejected_translation: The protocol was compiled by all the rules.
defect_description: 'Протокол' in administrative context is an official report/record; 'protocol' is a false friend.

chosen_translation: The declaration was filed on time.
rejected_translation: The declaration was declared on time.
defect_description: 'Подана' means filed/submitted; 'declared' is a circular false calque.

source: Квитанция выдана кассиром и подтверждает оплату.
chosen_translation: The receipt was issued by the cashier and confirms the payment.
rejected_translation: The receipt was issued by the cashier.
defect_description: Second clause confirming payment dropped.

source: Несмотря на очередь, он получил документы в тот же день.
chosen_translation: Despite the queue, he received the documents the same day.
rejected_translation: He received the documents the same day.
defect_description: Concessive clause 'несмотря на очередь' dropped.

source: Прием граждан ведётся по предварительной записи.
chosen_translation: Citizens are seen by appointment.
rejected_translation: Receiving of citizens is conducted by preliminary record.
defect_description: 'По предварительной записи' = by appointment; 'by preliminary record' is a false calque.

source: Ему нужно поставить штамп в паспорт.
chosen_translation: He needs to have his passport stamped.
rejected_translation: To him there is needed to put a stamp into the passport.
defect_description: Dative 'ему нужно' requires 'he needs'; causative 'have his passport stamped' required.

chosen_translation: City transport runs on schedule.
rejected_translation: Urban transport goes by schedule.
defect_description: Transport 'runs' not 'goes'; 'on schedule' not 'by schedule'.

chosen_translation: There is a lot of traffic in the city centre.
rejected_translation: In the city centre there are many traffic jams.
defect_description: 'Много пробок' can be rendered as 'a lot of traffic'; 'many traffic jams' is also correct but less natural.

chosen_translation: The playground is closed for renovation.
rejected_translation: The children's playground is closed on repair.
defect_description: 'Closed for renovation' requires 'for', not 'on'; the modifier is redundant.

chosen_translation: The municipality is responsible for street cleanliness.
rejected_translation: The municipality is responsible for cleanliness of streets.
defect_description: Compound noun 'street cleanliness' is more natural than genitive 'cleanliness of streets'.

chosen_translation: He lives in a residential area.
rejected_translation: He lives in a sleeping district.
defect_description: 'Спальный район' means residential/suburban area; 'sleeping district' is a false literal.

chosen_translation: The shop sign is outdated.
rejected_translation: The signboard on the shop is obsolete.
defect_description: 'Устарела' for a sign means outdated; 'obsolete' implies no longer functioning.

source: Светофор не работает на этом перекрёстке.
chosen_translation: The traffic light is out of order at this intersection.
rejected_translation: The traffic light does not work on this crossroads.
defect_description: 'Out of order' is the natural English idiom for broken equipment; 'crossroads' is British English; 'intersection' is more standard.

source: Парковка запрещена с семи до девяти утра.
chosen_translation: Parking is prohibited from seven to nine in the morning.
rejected_translation: Parking is forbidden from seven till nine in the morning.
defect_description: 'Prohibited' is the standard term for traffic/civic regulations; 'from...to' is preferred over 'from...till' in formal notices.

source: Он снял квартиру недалеко от метро.
chosen_translation: He rented a flat near the metro.
rejected_translation: He removed an apartment not far from the subway.
defect_description: 'Снял квартиру' means rented a flat; 'removed' is a false calque; 'метро' can be metro.

chosen_translation: The housing question is pressing.
rejected_translation: The residential question stands sharply.
defect_description: 'Стоит остро' means is pressing/acute; 'stands sharply' is a false literal calque.

chosen_translation: The utility debt is growing.
rejected_translation: The debt on communal services grows.
defect_description: 'Коммуналка' = utilities; 'communal services' is a literal calque; present progressive preferred for ongoing growth.

source: Дорога строилась два года, и в итоге её открыли досрочно.
chosen_translation: The road was under construction for two years, and in the end it was opened ahead of schedule.
rejected_translation: The road was under construction for two years.
defect_description: Second clause about early opening dropped.

source: Он обратился в горсовет с жалобой.
chosen_translation: He filed a complaint with the city council.
rejected_translation: He addressed himself to the city council with a complaint.
defect_description: 'Обратился с жалобой' = filed a complaint; 'addressed himself to' is non-standard.

chosen_translation: The bus route was changed.
rejected_translation: The route of bus was changed.
defect_description: 'Bus route' is a compound noun; 'route of bus' lacks article and uses wrong structure.

source: Контролёр проверил билеты у всех пассажиров.
chosen_translation: The inspector checked all passengers' tickets.
rejected_translation: The controller checked tickets at all passengers.
defect_description: 'Контролёр' on transit is an inspector/ticket checker; 'controller' is a false friend.

source: Нарушитель заплатил штраф и был предупреждён повторно.
chosen_translation: The violator paid the fine and was warned again.
rejected_translation: The violator paid the fine.
defect_description: Second clause about the warning dropped.

chosen_translation: Utility bills go up every year.
rejected_translation: Communal services become more expensive every year.
defect_description: 'Дорожать' for bills means go up; 'utility bills' is the natural English term.

chosen_translation: The lift is out of order. Please use the stairs.
rejected_translation: The elevator is broken. Use the staircase.
defect_description: 'Out of order' is the standard notice; 'Please use' is more polite in public signage.

source: Посетитель написал жалобу в книгу отзывов.
chosen_translation: The visitor wrote a complaint in the feedback book.
rejected_translation: The visitor wrote a complaint in the book of reviews.
defect_description: 'Книга отзывов' is a complaints/feedback book; 'book of reviews' is a literal calque.

source: Пешеходная зона введена в прошлом году.
chosen_translation: The pedestrian zone was introduced last year.
rejected_translation: Pedestrian zone was entered in last year.
defect_description: 'Введена' for a policy means introduced; 'entered in' is a literal mistranslation; article missing.

source: Он нашёл работу через центр занятости.
chosen_translation: He found a job through the employment centre.
rejected_translation: He found work through the centre of employment.
defect_description: 'Работу' in job context is 'a job'; 'employment centre' is the standard compound noun.

source: В нашем городе хороший общественный транспорт.
chosen_translation: Our city has good public transport.
rejected_translation: In our city there is good public transport.
defect_description: 'Our city has' is more natural for general description; both are acceptable but 'has' is preferred.

chosen_translation: The street lighting broke down.
rejected_translation: The street illumination went out of order.
defect_description: 'Освещение' is lighting not illumination; 'broke down' is more natural than 'went out of order'.

source: Мэр открыл новый парк в центре города.
chosen_translation: The mayor opened a new park in the city centre.
rejected_translation: The mayor has opened new park in the centre of city.
defect_description: Simple past for completed one-time event; articles required; 'city centre' as compound noun.

source: Доступ в здание ограничен для посторонних.
chosen_translation: Access to the building is restricted to outsiders.
rejected_translation: Access into building is limited for strangers.
defect_description: 'Access to' is correct; definite article required before 'building'; 'посторонних' = unauthorised persons.

chosen_translation: The line is busy.
rejected_translation: The telephone line is occupied.
defect_description: 'Занята' for a phone line means busy; 'occupied' is used for rooms/seats.

chosen_translation: All counters are busy; you will have to wait.
rejected_translation: All windows are occupied, you will need to wait.
defect_description: 'Окошко' at a service desk is a counter; 'occupied' applied to counters is non-standard.

source: Несмотря на закрытие офиса, они получили нужные документы, так как воспользовались онлайн-порталом.
chosen_translation: Despite the office being closed, they obtained the documents they needed, as they used the online portal.
rejected_translation: Despite the office being closed, they obtained the documents they needed.
defect_description: Causal clause about using the online portal dropped.

chosen_translation: The administration building was renovated.
rejected_translation: The administration building was repaired.
defect_description: Full building work is renovation; 'repaired' implies fixing specific damage.

chosen_translation: The permit has expired.
rejected_translation: The term of action of the permission has expired.
defect_description: 'Срок действия разрешения истёк' = 'the permit has expired'; the compound noun is the natural form.

chosen_translation: The hot water has been turned off until Friday.
rejected_translation: Hot water is switched off till Friday.
defect_description: Definite article required; present perfect passive appropriate for recently-enacted state; 'until' preferred over 'till' in notices.

source: Новый торговый центр открылся на прошлой неделе, и уже полон посетителей.
chosen_translation: The new shopping centre opened last week and is already full of visitors.
rejected_translation: The new shopping centre opened last week.
defect_description: Second clause about being full of visitors dropped.
